gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price. iCloud+ 2 TB costs $9.99 a month ($119.88 a year) in the US. The cheapest UGREEN NAS we priced costs $239.99 without drives, or two years of that plan. And keeping a full 2 TB off-site copy on Backblaze B2 at $6.95/TB a month costs $13.90 a month, which is more than the iCloud plan it would replace.
standout_why: I opened two of ChatGPT's cited pages. Apple's 'Backup methods for iPhone or iPad' (support.apple.com/en-us/108771) gives only capacity limits ('up to 12 TB', 14 TB with Apple One Premier), with no plan price and no hardware cost. When fetched, Synology's iOS Photos KB page (kb.synology.com/.../SynologyPhotos/iPhone) showed no price, no NAS model and no hardware requirement. Of the other cited pages, ChatGPT's own excerpts show Apple's 'Set up and use iCloud Photos' and Synology's 2023 Photos blog post are about features. I didn't open them myself. ChatGPT's 'Synology DiskStation NAS' card had no price in the answer, and the answer gives no cost or payback figure. Our current page has a DS225+ range from early November that I could not re-read today and a BeeStation figure it marks 'not read live'.
decides: This confirms 'replace part of it, keep a small iCloud plan' rather than 'cancel iCloud'. Before drives, the NAS box alone equals 2 to 3.25 years of the 2 TB plan (UGREEN DH2300 $239.99 ÷ $119.88/yr ≈ 2.0 yr; DXP2800 $389.99 ≈ 3.25 yr). A proper off-site copy in Backblaze B2 then costs more each month than iCloud+ 2 TB. So the NAS saves money only if the off-site copy is a drive the family owns, kept somewhere else. For a family that wants the lowest cost, the cheapest box (DH2300) plus an owned off-site drive is the only route that clearly beats $9.99 a month inside about three years.

findings.label: Warranty and usable capacity
findings.value: 3-year warranty; 8 TB model has about 6.98 TB usable (4 TB BeeStation about 3.45 TB)
findings.note: Usable capacity is from bee.synology.com. The 3-year warranty is from https://www.synology.com/en-us/store/BST170-8T, read the same day. Neither Synology page showed a USD price in the fetched content. It loses because it has a single drive and no RAID, so one drive failure loses the local copy.

findings.label: Off-site copy cost, Backblaze B2
findings.value: $6.95 per TB per month; first 10 GB free; no minimum file size or storage duration
findings.note: Arithmetic: a 2 TB off-site copy costs 2 × $6.95 = $13.90 a month, which is $3.91 a month more than iCloud+ 2 TB ($9.99). So a NAS plus B2 off-site copy never pays back against iCloud+ 2 TB on running cost alone.
